# Restructure the waybar converge widget as a status view of the rebuild machinery

Ruling from the owner (2026-08-25): the widget must stop reconstructing the host's state from
the outside and instead render state the rebuild machinery itself authors at each transition.
When the webhook fires to say cosmo is ahead, that authors a state change; when the build
starts, another; success/failure, another; the reboot detector's verdicts, the same. The widget
becomes a projection of that authored state, pushed to the bar when it changes — not a 30-second
poll that re-derives everything (including a `git ls-remote` round trip to GitHub per tick,
which the current widget does).

Target repo: cosmo (normal GitHub PR flow). Branch + PR as usual.

## Current machinery — read all of these first

- `hosts/classic-laddie/default.nix`:
  - `github-relay` config: push webhook on patflynn/cosmo main → `systemctl start
    cosmo-rebuild.service` (polkit grant scoped to exactly that verb+unit).
  - `systemd.services.cosmo-rebuild` (~line 435): oneshot converge loop — `git ls-remote` the
    tip, compare `/var/lib/cosmo-rebuild/deployed-rev` (written ONLY on successful switch),
    `nixos-rebuild switch --flake github:patflynn/cosmo/$rev`, loop up to 5x. Hourly
    `cosmo-rebuild.timer` as belt-and-braces.
- `modules/common/auto-reboot.nix` + `auto-reboot-scripts.nix`: `reboot-needed` detector
  (hourly + OnBootSec=5min + RandomizedDelaySec=5m, also triggered onSuccess/onFailure of
  cosmo-rebuild) writes/clears `/var/lib/reboot-pending/{state,last-blocked}`; `reboot-attempt`
  daily quiet-window reboot. Scripts live outside the module so `auto-reboot-test.nix` drives
  the real ones against canned trees via env-overridable roots — keep that pattern.
- `home/scripts/waybar-converge.nix` + `waybar-converge-test.nix`, `home/waybar.nix`: the
  current widget — one batched ssh per 30s poll gathering deployed-rev, remote tip, unit
  active/failed, a journal line, reboot state; derives states
  rebuilding > failed > unreachable > reboot-overdue > reboot-pending > current > stale.

## The redesign

### 1. The converge unit authors a status file

`/var/lib/cosmo-rebuild/status` (key=value lines, same idiom as the reboot state files),
written atomically (tmp+mv) at every transition:

- Unit start, tip resolved, deploy decided: `phase=building` + `target=<rev>` +
  `deployed=<prev-rev-or-empty>` + `at=<epoch>`. The webhook's "cosmo is ahead" becomes visible
  the instant the relay starts the unit — this is the state the owner asked for by name.
- Each successful switch: `phase=current` + `rev=<rev>` + `at=<epoch>`. The existing
  `deployed-rev` file keeps its exact semantics (the ledger, written only on success); status
  is a projection beside it, never a replacement.
- A run that finds tip == deployed refreshes `phase=current` + `checked=<epoch>` — the widget
  learns "last verified against the remote at T" without ever doing its own ls-remote.
- Failure: `phase=failed` + `target=<rev>` + `at=<epoch>` + a one-line `detail=`. Author this
  from `ExecStopPost` (reads `$SERVICE_RESULT`/`$EXIT_STATUS`) rather than a trap in the
  script, so timeouts and kills are captured, not just `bash -e` aborts. ExecStopPost runs on
  success too — make it a no-op when the script already wrote a terminal phase.
- `phase=failed` with `target != deployed` IS the behind state: laddie knows main moved and
  knows it isn't running it. Do not add any GitHub polling anywhere on the widget path.

Factor the converge script out of the host module the way `auto-reboot-scripts.nix` did, with
env-overridable roots and command names, so a check can drive it with fake `git`/`nixos-rebuild`
bins and assert the status transitions.

### 2. A laddie-side renderer owns state derivation

A small script installed on classic-laddie (e.g. `converge-status`) reads
`/var/lib/cosmo-rebuild/status` + `/var/lib/reboot-pending/{state,last-blocked}` and emits the
single-line waybar JSON. State precedence stays: building > failed > reboot-overdue >
reboot-pending > current (with rev + age in tooltip); `stale` becomes "status file ancient or
absent" (machinery not running at all). Derivation logic lives in ONE place, on the host;
`unreachable` is the only state the workstation side may synthesize.

### 3. The workstation side becomes a stream, not a poll

`home/scripts/waybar-converge.nix` becomes: persistent ssh to laddie running `converge-status`
once, then `inotifywait -m` on the two state directories, re-rendering one JSON line per
event, plus a periodic timeout re-render (~5min) so tooltip ages stay honest and a dead pipe is
noticed. Waybar side (`home/waybar.nix`): continuous `exec` custom module (no `interval`),
`return-type: json`, each emitted line replaces the display. On ssh exit: emit `unreachable`
with the diagnostic (keep the current stderr-harvesting approach — it is good), then reconnect
with capped backoff, forever. inotify-tools must be present on laddie for the remote command —
reference the store path in the remote command or add it to the host's packages, whichever is
cleaner.

### 4. Fix today's live bug: stale reboot verdict after boot

The owner rebuilt, rebooted at 08:11, and the widget showed reboot-pending until the detector's
first post-boot run at 08:19 (OnBootSec=5min + RandomizedDelaySec=5m). The detector's own
comment promises "the run right after the reboot is how the state clears itself" — make that
true: run `reboot-needed.service` at boot directly (wantedBy multi-user.target or an immediate
OnBootSec/OnActiveSec without the randomized delay — pick the cleanest; the randomized delay
should keep applying to the hourly ticks). With the inotify stream, the clear reaches the bar
seconds after boot instead of minutes.

## Constraints

- Timers and the level-triggered converge loop stay exactly as they are — the status file is a
  projection the same loop authors, never a second control path.
- `deployed-rev` semantics untouched; `reboot-needed`/`reboot-attempt` logic untouched beyond
  the boot-time activation.
- No GitHub API or git polling from the workstation, and none added to the widget path.
- Match the repo's comment idiom: these modules carry design rationale in comments; keep them
  information-dense, no filler, no narration of the obvious.
- Update BOTH test files for the new shape and extend coverage: status-file transitions
  (building/current/failed incl. ExecStopPost-authored failure), renderer precedence, stream
  script's unreachable+reconnect path (drive with a fake ssh on PATH as the existing test
  does). Tests drive real scripts via env roots — no mocks of the logic itself.

## Acceptance

- `nix flake check` passes — PASTE the final output lines in your report; claims without pasted
  output are treated as not done.
- `git diff --stat` against main in the report.
- Report must state where each state transition is authored (which line of which unit writes
  which phase) so the owner can review the machinery as a state machine.
- Commit and push before starting long verification; never background a nix build and exit
  without committing.


# Correction: the new components are Go, not bash

The repo owner has ruled: this redesign is the graduation point for the converge machinery.
Everything NEW you were briefed to build — status authoring, renderer, watch stream — is one
small Go program, not shell. The overall design from the original brief stands unchanged; only
the implementation medium of the new parts changes. If you already wrote bash for them, discard
it; keep your reading and any nix wiring that still applies.

## The tool

One Go binary, `converge-status`, living in cosmo (pick a sensible spot for a Go package in
this flake, e.g. `pkgs/converge-status/` with `buildGoModule`; follow whatever Go layout the
repo already uses, or standard cmd/ layout if none). Three subcommands:

- `converge-status set phase=building target=<rev> ...` — author a transition: validate the
  phase and keys, write the status file atomically (tmp+mv). Called by the converge unit script
  and its ExecStopPost line. This makes the binary the single owner of the schema; nothing else
  ever writes the file.
- `converge-status render` — read the status file + `/var/lib/reboot-pending/{state,last-blocked}`,
  emit one waybar JSON line. All precedence logic (building > failed > reboot-overdue >
  reboot-pending > current; stale = status file ancient/absent) and age formatting lives here.
- `converge-status watch` — render once, then fsnotify on the two state directories, re-render
  one line per relevant event, plus a periodic re-render (~5min) so tooltip ages stay honest.
  Runs on classic-laddie, invoked over ssh by the workstation side.

State-dir paths and the reboot-overdue threshold come from flags with production defaults, so
tests point the binary at temp dirs — same philosophy as the env-overridable roots in
`auto-reboot-scripts.nix`.

## Dependencies and style

- fsnotify is the one permitted third-party dep. Nothing else — supply-chain minimalism is a
  first-order concern in this repo. Pin via go.mod/vendor as buildGoModule requires.
- Terse comments, high info-density. No package-doc essays; the design rationale stays in the
  nix modules' comments where it already lives.

## What stays shell (glue only)

- The converge unit script: shrinks to its existing loop with `converge-status set` calls at
  the transition points; still factored out of the host module for testability as briefed.
- ExecStopPost: one `converge-status set phase=failed ...` invocation guarded as briefed.
- The workstation waybar script: a minimal loop — ssh laddie `converge-status watch`; when ssh
  exits, emit one `unreachable` JSON line locally (keep the current widget's stderr-diagnostic
  harvesting for the tooltip) and reconnect with capped backoff. No logic beyond that loop;
  anything smarter belongs in the Go tool.
- `auto-reboot-scripts.nix` untouched except the boot-time activation fix from the original
  brief.

## Testing

- Go tests run the REAL built binary (or its cobra-less main via exec) against canned state
  dirs: schema round-trip (set → render), precedence table, failed-with-target≠deployed
  (the behind state), stale/absent file, watch emitting on a file move into a tempdir.
- Replace/adapt the bash test derivations (`waybar-converge-test.nix`) accordingly; keep
  `auto-reboot-test.nix` green. Integration over mocks: drive the binary, not stubbed funcs.

## Acceptance (unchanged from the original brief)

- `nix flake check` passes — PASTE the final output lines; claims without pasted output are
  treated as not done.
- `git diff --stat` against main in the report.
- Report the transition-authorship map: which line of which unit/script issues which
  `converge-status set`.
- Commit and push before long verification; never background a nix build and exit without
  committing.


# Note on lineage

A prior agent started this build and was lost to a quota interruption before committing
anything; you are starting clean. The two sections above are one brief: the first states the
redesign, the second the ruling that its new components are Go. Where they conflict on
implementation medium, the Go section wins.
